notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: no county commissioner, sheriff, clerk, assessor and treasurer candidates of Okfuskee County were matched to contributions reported to the Ethics Commission since 2023.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Oklahoma yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included. Residents also pay Okfuskee County.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
The city borrowed $20,007,000 during the year, which is not counted as revenue but helps explain spending above revenue.
Debt service leaves out $558,000 of principal repaid with new borrowing the city did not spend on capital that year, most likely refinancing or a rolled-over note.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: no candidates for mayor and council of City of Okemah were matched to contributions reported to the Ethics Commission since 2023.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
Cameras: no license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Okemah's borders in OpenStreetMap as of 2026-10-20.

A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Oklahoma yet.
